messages:
zara: Quick sync: I prototyped an alternative autoscaler signal that emits a compact "admission credit" vector per pool instead of publishing raw GPU counts. The goal is better packing for many small requests and clearer cost signals for routing. Link to draft: https://redwood.internal/rfc/630

nick: curious — how are credits different from tokens we've discussed earlier?

zara: similar idea but credits are typed and bounded: {short_cpu, short_gpu, long_gpu, kv}. Each credit type maps to an expected request class. Credits are fractional and come with a seq id + ttl.

elaine: important: keep preemption and hard SLA logic unchanged. Credits should be advisory for admission and only slightly influence soft-eviction. Hard evict still consults reserved_slots and lease metadata.

raj: operational questions: 1) heterogeneous GPU SKUs, 2) model affinity (A100-only), 3) stale snapshots. How do we avoid unsafe placements?

zara: answers: 1) include per-sku efficiency factors in the snapshot so credits -> effective-GPU-units; 2) each credit has an optional "sku_constraint" flag (if set, admission must match pool SKU); 3) snapshots carry seq+ttl — if stale, admission falls back to absolute published capacity. Also emit credit_staleness metric.

viv: propose a conservative scorer: soft_eviction_score = base_priority + preempt_penalty - alpha * min(effective_credit, cap) + beta * recent_cost_delta. Cap prevents credits from overpowering priority.

nick: what about billing/read ties? If cost_usd_hr is included, routing & billing must both read the same authoritative field. Also ensure we don't double-count during failover.

zara: agreed: snapshot includes cost_source id. Billing only reads cost when cost_source matches operator-master. Routing reads it otherwise but won't mutate billing records.

autoscaler-bot: Canary scheduled: admission-credits-canary on canary-4 at 2026-03-24T10:00Z. Telemetry: credit_staleness, eviction_churn_by_cause, p95_tail.

elaine: rollout checklist I want in the RFC followup: proto w/ seq+ttl, sku efficiency table, sku_constraint semantics, capped scorer impl, telemetry + dashboards, test matrix (mostly-small, mixed-large, prewarm burst), and rollback criteria (eviction_churn > 3x or p95 > 1.25x baseline).

raj: ops/UX note: add a debug-expanded sample row every minute (not everyone toggles debug) so SRE can inspect mappings. Also include a short example mapping: 0.02 short_gpu ~= 1 chat-turn; 0.6 long_gpu ~= large batch.

viv: agree — also add a "reserved_credit" boolean per tenant to shield hard SLAs from soft credit depletion.

zara: will add all that. I'll open the RFC patch with proto diff, scorer pseudo-code, dashboards, and rollout steps. tagging @elaine @nick @raj @viv for review.

autoscaler-bot: Canary metrics posted (first 12m): credit_staleness_med=1.2s, eviction_churn=0.8/10m, p95_tail +2.6% vs baseline. Dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.internal/d/credit-canary

zara: thanks everyone. Closing thread; DM me for urgent concerns.
